Title: Conception and pathogenesis of Cushing's disease
Abstract Note: The author's study on the conception and pathogenesis of Cushing's disease is based on a personal observation which is summarized as follows: A 24-year-old man among whose clinical antecedents must be noted that he never experienced any sexual impulse. Directly after typhoid contracted at the age of 11 years, he became extremely fat in the face and body, except for the limbs, showing a disproportion of growth between the body and the extremities, the latter remaining short and slender. The development of the penis and testes were delayed and presented infantile features. Four years after the typhoid, polyuria and nocturia without polydipsia developed, together with progressive muscular asthenia. At 22 years of age, a thoracic radicular syndrome of vertebral origin developed followed by the first signs of heart failure. With the diagnosis of cardiac insufficiency, the patient was admitted to hospital where he died shortly afterwards. In the course of investigation, the following outstanding signs were noted: 'A full moon' face with abundant panniculus adiposus, slight oedema, labial cyanosis and facial hirsutism; a short neck, thoracic and axillary hypertrichosis; a small thorax with abundant subcutaneous fat; a big globular hypotonic abdomen; 'striae cutis distensae purpurae' and copious pubescence on the abdominal and pubic regions; dry and scaly skin. Moist hypostatic râles in the lower right lung zone; tachycardia at a regular rate of 150; arterial pressure 170 mm/ 100 mm; hypertrophy of left ventricle; enlarged aortic arch; mitro-aortic murmur; acrocyanosis in hands and feet; congestive hepatomegaly; intense decalcification of the entire osseous system with platyspondylia of the second to sixth dorsal vertebrae and crush fractures of the fourth and fifth dorsal vertebrae; fasting blood glucose value two Gm; blood Ca. 0.112 Gm; and blood urea 0.35 Gm per 1,000. Necropsy: Hypertrophied and distended heart (700 Gm) especially in the left ventricle; aortic and coronary atheroma; diffused softening of the bones, which could be easily cut with the knife; suprarenal bodies hypertrophic (9 Gm each); pituitary gland of normal size but containing an adenoma of basophil cells with connective tissue and capillary hyperplasia; testicular atrophy. No abnormalities were found in the rest of the internal secretory system. The author conceives a difference between Cushing's disease and Cushing's syndrome. It is a disease when determined by an adenoma or a hyperfunction of the basophil cells of the pituitary, with or without tumorous formations. It is a syndrome when the original cause is other than the said hyperfunction (primary interrenalism, virilescent ovarian adenomata, thymic carcinoma etc.) The author passes on to a study of the physiogenesis of the diencephalon pituitary system to facilitate the comprehension of the pathogenesis of each of the signs appearing in his patient's syndromic picture. Obesity and the 'striae cutis distensae purpura' would result from reactional polycythemia and from the distension of the sub-papillary plexus while the erythrophoric hormone and the suprarenal cortex would account for the reddish hue of the striae and the melanophoric hormone for the dark brown skin which is sometimes a characteristic of these patients. The hypertrichosis would be of a cortico-suprarenal origin. The acrocyanosis would translate the dysfunction of the diencephalic vascular centre into a hypotony of the tuber's thermoregulating centre. Dysmorphic obesity might result either from the dysfunction of the diencephalic centre of fat metabolism, or from a hypersecretion of Ansehnino and Hoffmann's hormone or from the inhibitory action of Lucke's contra-insular hormone from the hyposecretion of Raab's lipoithryn. Penile and testicular hypotrophy and the absence of sexual impulse may be due to the hypersecretion of adenohypophyseal gonadotrophic hormone at a moment when, puberty having not yet made its appearance, the genitals are in process of full evolution, or to the inhibitory action of the suprarenal cortex on the gonadotrophic secretion of the basophil pituitary. The gonadal hyporunction would also account for the slender, womanlike hands and feet and for the feminine tone of the voice. The osteoporosis and the increased blood calcium would be due to the restrained osteoclastic activity of the bone, with no alteration operative in the osteoclastic function. Arteriosclerotic factors would be the same as those determining the deranged fat metabolism. In high blood pressure pathogenesis there must be noted a psychical nervous factor located in the brain cortex and diencephalon, an endocrine factor. The strain asthenia and apathy have a double source: the alteration of the endocrine-vegetative tone of cortico-diencephalic type and the distorted metabolism of carbohydrates. The radicular pains originate from the reduction of the intervertebral foramina due to the platyspondylia. The dyspnoea and other symptoms of heart failure are due to the functional and organic alterations of the myocardium originated by coronary insufficiency. The polyuria might be caused by either a dysfunction of the diencephalic hydroregulating centre or a hyposecretion of the anti-diuretic principle. Hyperglycaemia, (with or without glycosuria), might be due to hypersecretion of the contra-insular hormone, hyposecretion of the pancreotrophic hormone, hyperproduction of the cortical hormone or to a diencephalic (hypothalamic) dysfunction. The increased blood cholesterol parallel to deranged general fat metabolism would originate from a hyperfunction of the suprarenal cortex in relation with the hypersecretion of adrenocorticotrophic hormone. Sixty-eight bibliographical references are added. Author.

Title: The Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Abstract Note: A 27-year-old man stated that since childhood his skin had been extremely sensitive to blows. The fingers and toes, short and thick, were capable of active and passive hyperextension. The metacarpal and metatarsal bones were readily movable; the skin of the whole body and of the head possessed an exaggerated elasticity. The blood calcium was 14.8 mgm % and the cholesterol 127 mgm %.

Title: Progressive scleroderma with sclerodactylia
Abstract Note: A case of scleroderma in a man aged 24 is described. The disease began one year previously with paraesthesiae and the development of hard areas in the skin. Later this spread, involving larger areas of skin; eventually the condition was generalized with diffuse pigmentation. The blood calcium was 16 mgm per cent and the sodium 280 mgm per cent. The blood cholesterol was 2.19 Gm per 1,000. The author decided against thyroidectomy, but because of signs suggesting an adrenal deficiency (asthenia, hypotension, melanoderma) gave potassium iodide, ammonium chloride, adrenal extract (cortiron, percorten), adrenaline, vitamin C and local application of an iodized cold cream.

Title: A case of systemic fat embolism in the course of intramedullary nailing. clinical, anatomical and pathogenetic considerations
Abstract Note: The case history is presented of a man aged 38 with a fracture of the femur, who developed fat- embolism following a Ktintscher- nail reposition. Arguments are listed against the supposition that the embolie fat originates from the site of the fracture; the free interval may last up to 9 days, and the marrow- fat contains less than 1% of cholesterol, whereas the embolie fat shows the presence of up to 30% cholesterol and cholesterol- esters. Equally, the hypercalcémia and anemia on the 2nd and 3rd day remain unexplained by the unsophisticated mechanical theories of the pathogenesis. The treatment is outlined.

Title: Effect of calcium deficiency on serum lipids in man -
Abstract Note: To ascertain the effects of calcium deficiency on serum levels of cholesterol, phospholipids, triglycerides, and free fatty acids in man, the authors maintained two subjects on a nutritionally adequate diet with calcium intake reduced to 87 mg/day and 95 mg/day for OO days. For one subject (OG) mineral balances during the 60 days were calcium -5Jg, magnesium + 7.9 g, phosphorus + 4.9 g. The other subject (RC) had a subtotal gastrectomy which would further exaggerate mineral losses; his balances were calcium - 17.9 g, magnesium - 1.4 g, and phosphorus - 43 g. Both subjects were in nitrogen equilibrium. Dietary fat was predominantly animal fat Total fecal lipids, serum calcium and serum phosphorus did not change appreciably during the study. The serum lipid levels were variable and did not follow any specific trend except for the phospholipids and triglycerides which showed a decrease from control levels by the end of the deficiency period. In spite of the close association of calcium deficiency and elevated serum lipids in animals, the authors could not demonstrate such a relationship in man. This may be due to the presence of more efficient mechanisms for mobilizing calcium in man.

Title: Comparative aspects of hyperadrenocorticism and arteriosclerosis
Abstract Note: Repeatedly bred rats will develop a fatty liver and hyperlipidemia, hyperglycemia, hypertension, nephrosclerosis, hypercalcemia and nephrolithiasis, and arteriosclerosis, age prematurely, and die, often as a result of myocaidial infarction. These animals are obese and kyphotic, a reasonable facsimile of Cushing's disease. One of the most salient features of these spontaneously appearing degenerative changes is the progressive pituitary gland basophilia and adrenocortical hyperplasia. It is tempting to incriminate the abnormal steroidogenic activity of repeatedly bred rats as the prime vector responsible for the cushingoid habitus and the pathogenesis of the arterial degenerative changes. Mention is also made of the accelerated development of arteriosclerosis, myocardial infarction, premature aging, and death in spawning Pacific salmon. The salmon stores energy in the form of hepatic lipids, which, as the salmon fight their way upstream, without benefit of food or rest, are released, increasing the serum cholesterol levels from zero to 1,000 mg/100 ml. These fish develop hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hypercalcemia, adrenocortical hyperplasia, thymus gland involution, and a host of other abnormal metabolic and degenerative changes reminiscent of those seen in repeatedly bred rats, parturient females, and cushingoid patients. An attempt should be made to equate the metabolic consequences of the hyperadrenocorticism of the reproductive effort in fish, rat, and man. Scientists concerned with the problem of atherosclerosis, whether from the standpoint of carbohydrate, lipid, thrombosis, connective tissue metabolism, or stress, should be aware of the swelling tide of information regarding circadian rhythms, neurohormonal mechanisms, and their ubiquitous effects.

Title: Preliminary survey of lipid disorders and the development of corneal arcus among a group of Haitians
Abstract Note: The relation of corneal arcus to abnormalities of several biochemical parameters indicative of metabolic disorders was studied in a survey of 28 Negroes from Haiti, 18-41 yr old, of both sexes. Corneal arcus was not found to be associated with high levels of plasma lipids and lipoproteins, glucose or uric acid. The mean level of plasma cholesterol and triglycerides was noticeably lower than that of a group of Canadians of comparable age. The mean calcium level of the sample was 11 mg/100 ml, which is in the range of hypercalcemia according to North American standards (9.5-10.5 mg/100 ml). It is suggested that in Negroes from Haiti at least, the development of corneal arcus might be genetically determined rather than the reflexion of lipid disorders. However, in view of the small size of the sample, the results of this preliminary survey must be interpreted with caution.

Title: Hereditary osteopetrosis of the rabbit. I. General features and course of disease; genetic aspects. II. X-ray, haematologic, and chemical observations. III, Pathologic observations; skeletal abnormalities. IV. Pathologic observations; general features
Abstract Note: I. A series of papers worth reading for every pathologist specializing in bone pathology. Hereditary osteopetrosis in rabbits is a novelty. It was discovered by chance in a rabbit strain and followed up in 169 litters obtained by interbreeding as soon as the hereditary character of the disease had manifested itself. By out-crossing with unrelated stocks an F1 generation and later on an F2 generation were obtained. The disease is present at birth and is uniformly fatal. The survival period of most of the 293 cases was 4 to 5 weeks. In the first of the 4 papers the general conditions of the diseased animals are described. The outward manifestations are a peculiar malformation of the incisor teeth, retarded and arrested growth, later on malnutrition, loss of weight and cachexia. Hydrocephalus and exophthalmos were observed in a number of cases. Heredity is determined by the expression of a simple recessive unit factor; the affected individuals are homozygous for the factor. Heterozygous animals (transmitters) are identified only by breeding tests. The condition is not sex-linked. II. The results are given of X-ray, haematological and chemical studies on the rabbits with osteopetrosis. The X-ray picture, especially of the older animals, resembles very closely that of osteopetrosis (marble bone disease) in man. Haematological examinations were carried out by single and repeated counts on a large number of diseased animals and normal litter mates in the age range of 1 to 39 days. Progressively developing macrocytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and a moderate myeloid leucocytosis were the general features. Other abnormal findings were high reticulocyte and normoblast counts, anisocytosis and poikilocytosis, and degenerative changes of the neutrophils and lymphocytes. These changes were likewise present in all the animals under control. The chemical studies showed very low serum calcium values, low serum phosphorus values during the first 4 weeks of life, and elevated serum phosphatase values. The blood sugar content was low, blood cholesterol values were high. The liver glycogen was reduced especially in older cases, whereas muscle glycogen was only slightly lower than normal. III. The post-mortem findings are described in detail. The histological picture of the bones of the diseased rabbits is exactly the same as has been described time and again for osteopetrosis (marble bone disease) in man. It may be noted that the presence of osteoblasts, overlooked by a number of authors, is duly emphasized. All the bones were invariably and similarly affected. The condition is attributed to a primary disorder of the mesenchymal cells. IV. Other general features were: a very marked disturbance of phosphatase and calcium distribution in the tissues of many inner organs, depletion of glycogen in various tissues, and certain changes in endocrine glands. The thyroid showed a predominantly acidophilic reaction of the colloid; in the pituitary gland the proportion of basophilic cells was increased, and the adrenals showed a relative increase in the size of the medulla together with a greater content of fat in the cells of the cortex. The amount of parathyroid tissue identified microscopically, that is the glands themselves and dispersed accessory foci of parathyroid tissue in their neighbourhood, greatly exceeded that of normal rabbits. The parathyroid cells themselves showed no abnormal features, but sometimes cysts containing cellular débris were found. Other findings agreed with the anaemic condition of the animals, such as extramedullary haemopoietic foci, lymphoid hyperplasia and the occurrence of haemosiderin in the liver, spleen and lymph nodes. In conclusion, it is pointed out that the large amount of parathyroid tissue in osteopetrosis cases suggests a state of hyperparathyroidism, whereas low serum calcium, high phosphorus and phosphatase levels and a prominently osteoblastic reaction are suggestive of hypoparathyroidism. However, before an explanation of the part played by the parathyroid in this disease can be produced, other data, including particularly embryological studies, must be available. An interpretation of other endocrine gland changes must await additional information. An adequate bibliography is added to each of the 4 papers.

Title: Investigations on the toxicity of DDT for man
Abstract Note: Five workmen engaged in insect-destruction work using DDT were examined. They had been exposed for a long time to solutions and atmospheres containing a high concentration of DDT. In no cases were there any subjective manifestations of organic lesions corresponding to functional or organic liver damage: the blood prothrombin, cholesterol and sugar were normal and the urine showed no bile pigments or salts. The blood calcium was unchanged. The blood - was free from any changes in haemoglobin or cells which - would suggest an affection of the haematopoietic system. No subjective or organic affection of the nervous system was detectable. These men, thus, had suffered no ill-effects during the time (several years) that they had been working with DDT, although they had sometimes been exposed to the insecticide for ten hours at a stretch. It is presumed, therefore, that DDT is rapidly eliminated from the organism or that an organic detoxicating mechanism exists.
ExclusionReason: Neither serum cholesterol or calcium were changed

Title: An unusual case c f fatal hepatic sarcoidosis
Abstract Note: Although sarcoidosis presents liver involvement in upwards of 76% of cases at biopsy, jaundice is uncommon and death from hepatic sarcoidosis is extremely rare. A man of 48, however, complained of pruritus, having jaundice for one month. The liver was sharp, smooth, firm and slightly tender, 3 finge r breadths below the umbilicus, and the spleen was enlarged and hard. Alkaline phosphatase was 104 U., total cholesterol 700 mg. /100 ml. of which 130 mg, was esterified, serum globulin 3.3 g. /100 ml. and total bilirubin elevated, the more in the 'direct' fraction. Serum calcium was not elevated. Liver biopsy showed granulomatous formation. A laparotomy was performed to rule out obstructive jaundice and the biopsy specimen at operation was consistent with sarcoidosis. Giant cells contained Schaumann bodies. ACTH and cortisone were both tried and the clinical course worsened on this therapy. It was felt that the steroids might have caused an accelerated change from granulomatous picture to one of diffuse fibrosis and hyalinization. The resultant scarring damaged the parenchyma so markedly that hepatic insufficiency and death resulted. Zoeckler - Des Moines, la.

Title: Metabolic effects of controlled jejunocolic bypass
Abstract Note: Observations on the metabolic effects of Jejunocolic bypass in 11 grossly obese patients have been presented. The lengths of jejunum selected for anastomosis was 15 in. (4 patients), 20 in. (5 patients) and 25 in. (2 patients). Weight loss was noted in all patients and occurred most rapidly in the 15-inch-bypass patients. It was directly proportional to the amount of fat excreted in the stool. Diarrhea was a problem in all patients but stabilized within 6 to 12 mth after bypass. Xylose studies showed improvement after 6 to 12 mth due to prolonged transit time and compensatory increases in absorption power of the jejunum. Glucose tolerance curves were flattened as in other series and remained flattened. I. v. glucose tolerance tests showed 2 frankly diabetic patients to maintain a diabetic pattern postoperatively despite a flattened oral glucose tolerance curve. Fat excretion was inversely proportional to the length of jejunum used for the bypass. Serum cholesterol and total serum lipids were decreased to 40% to 50% of preoperative values and remained so. Cholesterol esters remained unchanged. Plasma protein levels were decreased immediately after bypass but became normal with stabilization of weight. Electrolyte difficulties were associated with anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. In one patient, a low serum calcium level which led to tetany was corrected by raising the serum albumin with the intravenous administration of normal human serum albumin. Gastric secretion studies were essentially unchanged by the bypass. Pulmonary function improved with weight loss in all patients. The 2 patients with alveolar hypoventilation syndrome reverted to a normal ventilation/ perfusion pattern. Liver function studies which were abnormal immediately after operation all became normal with time. Liver structure remained essentially unchanged except in 2 patients. One patient had continuity of bowel restored for marital and psychological difficulties. One death occurred in these series and is considered to be due to hepatitis. The jejunocolic bypass is a drastic measure for controlling obesity but, in a carefully selected few patients, it may be justified.

Title: Biological and analytic components of variation in long term studies of serum constituents in normal subjects. IV. Results of a study designed to eliminate long term analytic deviations
Abstract Note: Blood was sampled from 9 healthy subjects weekly for 10 wk, under controlled conditions. Eighteen serum constituents were measured in duplicate in each sample on a single occasion. In this way analytic variation was minimized. Considerable variations in mean values and standard deviations of results were observed among the subjects. Physiological control of serum calcium and magnesium concentrations appeared to be more precise than duplicate determinations in the laboratory. Compared with a previous study from this laboratory, significantly different estimates of personal variation were noted for sodium, chloride, urea nitrogen, cholesterol, and LDH in a group matched by age, race, and sex. At the same time, the present study group, homogenous with respect to these demographic factors (and also occupation) showed as great a diversity in the mean concentrations of most constituents as was seen earlier in a larger, more heterogenous group of normal individuals. These findings indicate that certain blood parameters depend more on personal characteristics than on broad demographic factors.
ExclusionReason: Neither serum cholesterol or calcium were changed

Title: Reference values for serum total calcium and magnesium determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometry
Abstract Note: Reference values in the form of 95% ranges for serum calcium and magnesium using material from 196 males and females are presented. These included persons aged 2 days to 83 yr, apparently healthy persons as well as patients suffering from a wide variety of ailments without significant effect on serum calcium and magnesium levels. Measurements of serum urea, inorganic phosphate, proteins, cholesterol and alkaline phosphatase were made to screen the subjects for abnormalities in any of these measurements. One sample had to be excluded because of a moderately elevated blood urea. Three other samples had to be discarded for technical reasons - 2 because of visible hemolysis and 1 because the serum was insufficient for the whole range of tests. Applying standard tests no outliers were found. Using the nonparametric percentile method the reference (95%) range for serum calcium was found to be 8.4-10.8 mg/dl (in S.I. Units 2.1-2.7 mmol/L) and that for serum magnesium 1.6-2.4 mg/dl (in S.I. Units 0.70-1.0 mmol/L).
ExclusionReason: Neither serum cholesterol or calcium were changed

Title: The effect of agents interfering with soft tissue calcification and cell proliferation on calcific fibrous fatty plaques in rabbits
Abstract Note: The authors tested agents that might suppress the formation of fibrous plaques which are the significant lesions in human atherosclerosis. Six groups of rabbits were studied for 8 weeks: one group was fed a control diet and five groups received an atherogenic diet known to produce accumulations of connective tissue in arterial lesions. One group received only the atherogenic diet and the remaining four groups were treated simultaneously with the calcification inhibitor, ethane hydroxy diphosphonate (EHDP), at two dosage levels, as well as the antimitotic agent, N-desacetyl-N-methylcolchicine (Colcemid), or a combination of EHDP and Colcemid, respectively. None of the drugs reduced to normal the high serum cholesterol levels induced by the diet, but all reduced the elevated serum calcium concentrations occurring in untreated rabbits on the atherogenic diet. The lesions in the untreated group included marked accumulations of intra- and extracellular lipids (chiefly cholesterol) and calcium, as well as of glycosaminoglycans, collagen, and elastin. Aortic 'elastin' from these atherosclerotic rabbits had an increased content of polar amino acids, calcium, and cholesterol. Treatment with EHDP or Colcemid alone markedly inhibited these atherosclerotic processes, whereas combination therapy with both drugs completely suppressed all aspects of atherogenesis except for a few superficial lipid deposits close to the vessel lumen. The prevention of excessive deposition of arterial calcium by EHDP and also by Colcemid may play an important role in the antiatherogenic effect of these drugs.

Title: Role of mild excesses of vitamin D3 in arteriosclerosis. A study in squirrel monkeys
Abstract Note: Mild excesses of vitamin D3 were given to squirrel monkeys (Saimiri Sciureus) with and without hypercholesteremia for periods of 10 to 18 months. Blood chemistry of lipids, calcium and phosphorus was determined. The animals fed 0.5 p.100 cholesterol showed significant hypercholesteremia. Slight increases of serum calcium levels were observed only in the animals receiving 1,000 I.U. per day of vitamin D3. Most of the animals treated with excesses of vitamin D3 showed intimal thickening composed of prolifererating myointimal cells, collagen fibers and scattered cellular debris. Small doses (500 I.U. per day) of vitamin D3 produced intimal thickening composed of proliferating myointimal cells, collagen fibers debris. Higher doses (1,000 I.U. per day) of vitamin D3 produced more significant changes including fragmentation and duplication of the internal elastic membrane with spotty calcium deposits. The most significant lesions, similar to human arteriosclerosis, could be demonstrated in those animals receiving the combination of both 0.5 p. 100 cholesterol and 500 I.U. per day of vitamin D3. In in vitro studies, vitamin D2 and vitamin D3 demonstrated cytotoxic effects on cultured aortic smooth muscle cells. Because of the widespread use of vitamin D in the Western population which in general is mildly to moderately hypercholesteremic, this vitamin may be, in part, responsible for the current epidemic of arteriosclerosis in this population.

Title: The effect of wheat bran on serum cholesterol, serum triglyceride, serum calcium and serum total 3α hydroxy cholic acid and the duration of gastrointestinal transit (Danish)
Abstract Note: No changes in serum cholesterol, triglyceride, total 3α hydroxy cholic acid or serum calcium were observed in 25 pupil nurses following ingestion of approximately 24 g wheat bran (size of particles ≤1.7 mm, waterbinding capacity 5 g H2O/1 g bran). On the other hand, the duration of gastro intestinal transit was reduced and there was good correlation to increased frequency of defaecation. The body weight decreased significantly by an average of 0.430 kg. The daily calorie intake remained constant while the calcium intake increased significantly. Among the serum parameters and the dietary components, good correlation was found only between serum cholesterol and the dietary cholesterol content. In addition, the serum cholesterol proved to be inversely proportional to serum total 3α hydroxy cholic acid. The significance of this finding is not yet known.
ExclusionReason: Neither serum cholesterol or calcium were changed

Title: Lack of effect of bran enriched bread on plasma lipids, calcium, glucose and body weight
Abstract Note: The effects of a fibre-enriched diet upon 17 normal volunteers during a 5-week cross-over trial were studied. No change was found in body weight, blood glucose, plasma cholesterol, plasma triglycerides or serum calcium.
ExclusionReason: Neither serum cholesterol or calcium were changed

Title: Chronic hypercalcemia as a risk factor for coronary atherosclerosis
Abstract Note: Certain clinical and morphologic cardiac observations are described in 18 necropsy patients aged 18-58 years (mean age 45 years) (14 women with chronic hypercalcemia (11.6-34.4 mg/dl [mean 19.4 mg/dl]) for one to nine years (mean five years). Primary hyperparathyroidism was present in nine patients and secondary hyperparathyroidism in the other nine. Cardiac anular and extensive coronary arterial calcific deposits were present in ten patients (group 1) including four with considerable narrowing of two or three of the four major epicardial coronary arteries. Of the other eight patients (group 2), none had cardiac valve anular of cuspal calcific deposits, only two had coronary calcific deposits and they were small and did not cause significant luminal narrowing. Calcium was in the media of the coronary arteries in five patients. Comparisons of the patients in group 1 to those in group 2 disclosed similar mean ages, durations of hypercalcemia and serum-calcium levels, but significantly (P < .05) higher mean total serum-cholesterol levels (216 vs 163 mg/dl) and heart weights (426 vs 320 g). Thus, chronic hypercalcemia is associated with accelerated deposition of calcium in the cardiac anuli and valvular cusps, in the intima and media of coronary arteries, and in individual myocardial fibers. The coronary intimal calcium may produce luminal narrowing, especially in patients with serum total cholesterol levels > 200 mg/dl. Chronic hypercalcemia, therefore, may be viewed as a 'risk factor' for accelerated coronary atherosclerosis.

Title: The effect of local atmospheric temperature upon umbilical cord 25-hydroxy vitamin D
Abstract Note: There was a close correlation between 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD) measured in umbilical cord blood and both the mean monthly atmospheric temperature (P < 0.001) and the total hours of sunshine (P < 0.005) recorded during the last 3 months of pregnancy at the weather station nearest to the mother's home. Cord serum cholesterol also correlated with atmospheric temperature (P < 0.02) and sunlight (P < 0.009). No relationship was demonstrable between serum calcium and 25-OHD or between calcium or alkaline phosphatase and climatic conditions. Birth weight was linked positively with serum calcium (P < 0.0001) and inversely with alkaline phosphatase (P < 0.0001).

Title: Liposome entrapment enhances the hypocalcemic action of parenterally administered calcitonin
Abstract Note: The hypocalcemic effect of liposomal-entrapped calcitonin (CT) was evaluated in rats. Salmon CT and human CT were entrapped in liposomes composed of egg phosphatidylcholine with or without an equimolar amount of cholesterol. The liposomes were separated by Sepharose 4B chromatography into fractions consisting of large multilamellar vesicles and small unilamellar vesicles. The incorporation of CT was monitored by counting [125I]CT and by specific RIA. Liposomal entrapment enhanced the hypocalcemic potency of parenterally administered salmon CT and human CT. After iv administration, the large multilamellar vesicles were more potent than small unilamellar vesicles in their hypocalcemic effect; cholesterol inclusion in the MLV liposome preparation prolonged the hypocalcemia. However, with im administration, the cholesterol-free liposomes were more potent than their cholesterol-containing counterparts regardless of size. These studies demonstrate that liposomal entrapment can be used to enhance the hypocalcemic potency of CT. It appears that both the size and composition of the liposome preparation are important in this effect, as is the route of administration. It may be possible to produce liposome-CT preparations with advantageous pharmacological characteristics.

Title: Isotretinoin: A reappraisal
Abstract Note: Isotretinoin is remarkably effective in the treatment of severe cystic acne, however, many complications have been observed during treatment and new toxic effects have been reported. Hypertriglyceridemia associated with decreases in high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol has occurred in 25 percent of patients and requires monitoring during treatment. Painful erosions with granulation tissue recently have been reported in patients with severe acne. Other complications have included corneal opacities, pseudotumor cerebri, hypercalcemia, photosensitivity reactions, abnormal liver function tests, and skeletal hyperostosis. Isotretinoin is teratogenic and should be avoided during pregnancy. With the increasing acceptance and use of isotretinoin for cystic acne, as well as related disorders (inflammatory papulopustular acne with scarring, gram-negative folliculitis, and acne rosacea), a reevaluation of isotretinoin aimed at reducing complications is in order. Patient selection criteria and guidelines directed at reducing these complications are presented.

Title: A safe and effective approach to chronic constipation with a new product made from wheat husks: Fibraform (Testa triticum tricum)
Abstract Note: Fifty-two patients affected by chronic constipation were treated with a new product made from wheat husks characterized by a high fibre content (80%) and a very low content of phytate and energy value. A significant increase in stool frequency and an improvement in stool consistency was reported. Serum cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol and serum triglycerides showed significant changes, while no alteration in serum calcium concentration was observed.

Title: Hypothermia in the Japanese elderly
Abstract Note: A study of hypothermia in Tokyo Metropolitan Geriatric Hospital during a 6 year period revealed that axillary temperature of 79 patients (0.51% of total admitted patients and 3.8% of total died cases) have been 35.0% or less for at least 3 days. Mean age of the hypothermic patients, 80.2 years old, was higher than that of all admitted, 73.3 years old, or died cases, 76.8 years old. Disturbed consciousness (80%), generalized edema (44%), hypotension (27%) and bradycardia (14%) were associated with hypothermia. High frequency of abnormal laboratory findings was recognized in the hypothermic patients, low hemoglobin levels (less than 9 g/dl): 46%, low hematocrit levels (less than 30%): 60%, leukocytosis (more than 10000/mm3): 41%, thrombocytopenia (less than 100000/mm3): 61%, prolonged prothrombin time (more than 14 seconds): 79%, low fibrinogen levels (less than 200 mg/dl): 68%, high fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products levels (more than 10 μg/ml): 53%, hypoproteinemia (less than 5 g/dl): 47%, high GOT levels (more than 20 IU): 65%, high GPT levels (more than 20 IU): 36%, high LDH levels (more than 110 IU): 48%, hypocholesterolemia (less than 100 mg/dl): 39%, hypochloremia (less than 98 mEq/l): 45%, hypocalcemia (less than 7.5 mg/dl): 47%, high blood urea nitrogen levels (more than 30 mg/dl): 69%, high serum creatinine levels (more than 1.5 mg/dl): 41%, low serum triiodothyronine levels (less than 80 ng/dl): 92%, acidemia (pH<7.35), and atrial fibrillation: 32%. In one patient, J wave was recorded on electrocardiogram. Predominant clinical settings of hypothermia were cerebrovascular accidents (43%), pneumonia (34%), hypoproteinemia (33%), malignancy (28%) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (22%). The average survival period of the hypothermic patients was 20 days and about a half of cases died within 10 days after the onset of hypothermia. Serum total protein and total cholesterol levels in the former were significantly lower than those in the latter (p<0.01 and p<0.02, respectively). It was concluded that hypothermia was not infrequent in various morbid states commonly seen in the elderly and that the prognosis of hypothermia in the elderly was poor.

Title: Phase I evaluation of a synthetic mutant of β-interferon
Abstract Note: A synthetic mutant of β-interferon, produced by recombinant DNA technology, was prepared with serine substituted for the naturally occurring cysteine at amino acid 17. This molecule, after purification to homogeneity, was evaluated in 23 patients with cancer for tolerated doses, safety, and pharmacokinetics. Each patient was begun on twice weekly administration, one dose i.m., then an identical dose i.v. Doses, escalated weekly, were tolerated by 9 of 12 patients at 100 x 106 units i.m., 11 of 14 patients at 100 x 106 units i.v., and 8 of 10 patients receiving i.v. doses of 200 x 106 units. Fever (≥38.9° C), the commonest cause for ceasing dose escalation, occurred in 11 of 13 patients who developed limiting i.v. toxicity and 6 of 11 who developed limiting i.m. toxicity. Patients who did not have progressive cancer after completion of dose escalation received five consecutive daily doses at their maximum tolerated single dose by each route, i.m. and i.v. These two 5-day treatments were given without difficulty. All patients treated with 300 x 106 units or less, i.m. (n = 13) or i.v. (n = 10), were able to receive five daily doses without limiting toxicity. Peak serum titers occurred immediately after i.v. administration and declined in an exponential manner thereafter. Despite absence of measurable titers in serum after i.m. injection, fever and significant (P < 0.05) depression of WBC and platelet counts, serum calcium, and serum cholesterol occurred (prestudy to maximum tolerated dose). An immunoglobulin antibody to β-interferon, detected by enzyme-linked immunoabsorbent assay, developed in 17 of 23 patients. Neutralizing activity (titer 102) was found in only 1 of 23 patients. No immune-mediated sequelae (symptomatic or renal) were identified. Further Phase I and II trials with this molecule will determine whether it will prove to have a better therapeutic index or different spectrum of therapeutic activity from α-interferon or γ-interferon.

Title: Hyperuricaemia and risk of cardiovascular disease and overall death
Abstract Note: Serum uric concentration was determined in a series of 1462 women, aged 38-60 when first examined in 1968-69, as the first phase of longitudinal population study in Gothenburg, Sweden. Serum uric acid concentration was positively correlated to the 12-year overall mortality in univariate analysis. No relationship was observed between initial serum uric acid values and incidence of myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, ECG changes indicating ischaemic heart disease or stroke. The association between serum uric acid concentration and mortality was independent of age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, adipose tissue distribution, smoking habits, serum cholesterol concentration, serum triglyceride concentration, serum creatinine concentration, serum calcium concentration, use of diuretics, and haematological disease. The increased mortality could not be explained by any increase in malignant neoplastic disease.

Title: Lack of effect of drinking water barium on cardiovascular risk factors
Abstract Note: Higher cardiovascular mortality has been associated in a single epidemiological study with higher levels of barium in drinking water. The purpose of this study was to determine whether drinking water barium at levels found in some U.S. communities alters the known risk factors for cardiovascular disease. Eleven healthy men completed a 10-week dose-response protocol in which diet was controlled (600 mg cholesterol; 40% fat, 40% carbohydrate, 20% protein; sodium and potassium controlled at the subject's pre-protocol estimated intake). Other aspects of the subjects' lifestyles known to affect cardiac risk factors were controlled, and the barium content (as barium chloride) of the drinking water (1.5 L/day) was varied from 0 (first 2 weeks), to 5 ppm (next 4 weeks), to 10 ppm (last 4 weeks). Multiple blood and urine samples, morning and evening blood pressure measurements, and 48-hr electrocardiographic monitoring were performed at each dose of barium. There were no changes in morning or evening systolic or diastolic blood pressures, plasma cholesterol or lipoprotein or apolipoprotein levels, serum potassium or glucose levels, or urine catecholamine levels. There were no arrhythmias related to barium exposure detected on continuous electrocardiographic monitoring. A trend was seen toward increased total serum calcium levels with exposure to barium, which was of borderline statistical significance and of doubtful clinical significance. In summary, drinking water barium at levels of 5 and 10 ppm did not appear to affect any of the known modifiable cardiovascular risk factors.

Title: The antihypertensive effect of spironolactone and its effect on metabolism in elderly patients with essential hypertension
Abstract Note: Spironolactone was administered to 23 ambulatory patients with essential hypertension aged 54 to 85 years, of whom 70% were 60 years of older. 19 patients received 50 mg/day and 4 received 25 mg/day from weeks 4 to 16. Spironolactone reduced systolic, diastolic and mean blood pressures with no significant difference in response in different body positions. Pulse rate was not significantly altered. Comparison of 12 patients given spironolactone alone with 11 given the drug in combination with other antihypertensive drugs showed that the latter group was superior in the degree of blood pressure fall, overall improvement rate and utility rate. Serum potassium, magnesium and calcium levels and the sodium/potassium ratio were not significantly altered by administration of spironolactone, while serum sodium decreased significantly at weeks 4 and 16 and the serum calcium/magnesium ratio decreased significantly at week 16. Similarly, there were no significant alterations in serum total cholesterol, triglyceride, HDL-cholesterol or atherosclerosis index. Although serum creatinine changed significantly at week 8, the changes were within the normal range. Thus, even in patients of advanced age with essential hypertension, the administration of spironolactone 25 to 50 mg/day produced sufficient antihypertensive effect, with good overall improvement and quality-of-life ratings, with an incidence of hyperkalaemia of less than 10%.

Title: Normal range of various laboratory parameters in the aged
Abstract Note: In daily medical practice, it is important to know whether or not the normal ranges in the aged are different from those in the adult. Age-related changes in laboratory parameters were reviewed in this paper. In the hematologic parameters, red blood cell count and hemoglobin concentration decrease with age, while erythrocyte sedimentation rate and the levels of plasma fibrinogen increase. The levels of serum total protein and albumin decrease with age, while those of total cholesterol and triglycerides increase. Aging does not affect fasting blood glucose, but it impairs glucose tolerance. Serum urea nitrogen slightly increase with age-associated impairment of renal function. In contrast, serum creatinine does not often reflect the impairment of renal function. Reduction in muscle mass due to aging may offset the increase of creatinine in the elderly. Na, K, and Cl increase slightly with age. It should be noted that hypoalbuminemia, frequently associated with aging, lowers the levels of calcium. Correction of serum calcium levels with albumin concentration is required in hypoalbuminemia. Sex hormones, such as progesterone and estrogen, remarkably decrease with age in females. In males dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S), DHEA, and testosterone gradually decrease with age, and are considered to be useful indices for aging. Not only cross-sectional studies, but also longitudinal ones for each individual are required to confirm the age-related changes in laboratory parameters.

Title: Short-term effects of Org OD 14 and 17β-oestradiol on bone and lipid metabolism in early postmenopausal women
Abstract Note: The effects of 8 weeks of daily oral treatment with 1 mg 17β-oestradiol (E2). 2.5 mg Org OD 14 ((7α,17α)-17-hydroxy-7-methyl-19-norpregn-5(10)-en-20-yn-3-one), a steroid with weak androgenic, weak oestrogenic and weak progestational activity, or placebo on calcium and lipid metabolism were compared in 21 healthy, early post-menopausal women in a randomised double-blind study. The treatment period was followed by a treatment-free period of 8 weeks to stady the reversibility of drug-induced effects. The results show that both E2 and Org OD 14 reduce bone resorption, as indicated by the decreases in the urinary hydroxyproline/creatinine and calcium/creatinine ratios in 2-h fasting urine. In contrast to E2, Org OD 14 did not reduce serum calcium levels. As regards lipid parameters. E2 reduced the concentration of serum cholesterol and Org OD 14 decreased serum levels of high-density-lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides. All these effects appeared to be reversible after cessation of treatment. It is concluded that both of these steroids reduce bone resorption in early post-menopausal women, but that their mechanisms of action are most likely different.

Title: Nutrition evaluation of a sailing crew during a transatlantic race
Abstract Note: Few studies describe the nutritional status of people in stressful situations and with limited access to food. We assessed the dietary intake and serum indices of nutritional status in a sailing crew (n = 14) during a transatlantic race and in a control group (n = 11 males). The crew's mean energy intake was 13.3 MJ/d. In both groups, the intake of retinol, thiamin, riboflavin, vitamin C, calcium and iron was sufficient but the intake of vitamin B6, magnesium and zinc rather low. In sailors, serum HDL cholesterol was higher before the race (1.61 mmol/l; 95% confidence interval: 1.44-1.69) than after it (1.34 mmol/l; 1.26-1.43). Serum calcium, potassium, magnesium, ferritin, zinc, and selenium concentrations did not indicate nutritional deficiency in either group.

Title: Effect of calcification on in vivo mechanical response of rabbit arteries to balloon dilation
Abstract Note: Background. Atherosclerosis has been associated with loss of artery wall distensibility in human cadavers and in experimental animal models, giving it the lay term ''hardening of the arteries.'' Methods and Results. To assess the effect of calcification on arterial distensibility, balloon pressure and volume were recorded during dilation of calcified aortas in Watanabe heritable hyperlipidemic (WHHL) rabbits in vivo. Calcification was induced by dietary supplements of cholesterol, vitamin D2, and calcium. Balloon pressure, volume, and time signals were acquired at high frequency with controls for temperature and balloon inflation rate. Resistance to balloon dilation was minimal in control rabbit aortas (ΔV(max) = 5.0 ± 3.5 μl) and in excised nonatherosclerotic human coronary arteries, and it was small in aortas from cholesterol-fed rabbits (12.3 ± 8 μl), even when lipid levels were markedly elevated by a high cholesterol diet (611 ± 347 mg/dl). With dietary cholesterol, vitamin D2, and calcium supplements, WHHL rabbits developed mild hypercalcemia (15 ± 1.9 mg/dl), hypercholesterolemia (1,100 ± 633 mg/dl), moderate-to-marked aortic calcification, and high resistance to balloon dilation (38 ± 27) comparable to that seen in angioplasty patients. Conclusions. It is concluded that experimentally induced calcification decreases the distensibility of the rabbit aorta in vivo and that it yields to balloon dilation by plastic deformation closely resembling that seen in balloon angioplasty of human coronary arteries. These findings suggest that calcification contributes to arterial ''hardening'' associated with atherosclerosis.

Title: Total thyroidectomy for goiter
Abstract Note: Regarding non-toxic nodular goiter as a disease of whole thyroid gland and subtotal thyroidectomy as treatment without therapeutic rationale, the Authors present a comparative retrospective study of 228 thyroidectomyes: 108 subtotal (STT) and 120 total thyroidectomy (TT). Operative mortality was never observed in both series, inferior laringeal nerve palsy and permanent hypoparathyroidism not even. Temporary subclinic hypocalcemia was recorded in 39.8% of STT and in 47% of TT (n.s.) and temporary symptomatic hypocalcemia in none of STT and in 10% of TT (p < 0.01). Duration of postoperative hospitalization was the same in the two groups. 90 STT were followed up more than 3 years; relapse (ecography, scintigraphy) was observed in none of euthyrosic patients with hormonal therapy, in 10.7% of eutireosic without therapy, in 23% of hypothyreosic patients with therapy and in 78% in hypothyreosic without therapy. TT always allowed an easy control of clinical and subclinical (TSH, T3, T4, cholesterol, etc.).

Title: Metabolic disturbances in Plasmodium coatneyi-infected rhesus monkeys
Abstract Note: To investigate metabolic disturbances in an animal model of human malaria, four rhesus monkeys (Macaca mulatta) were infected with Plasmodium coatneyi, a parasite which induces cytoadherence of infected erythrocytes. When moribund or the parasitaemia had plateaued, the monkeys were sacrificed (3 animals) or treated with chloroquine (1 animal). Blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were sampled at intervals between inoculation and sacrifice or treatment. Arterial and CSF glucose and lactate rose during infection, indicating evolving insulin resistance. The arteriovenous difference in glucose concentration also increased, consistent with increased glucose consumption by parasitised tissues. Arterial plasma lactate rose but a positive arteriovenous concentration difference suggested tissue lactate uptake. The animal with the highest plasma lactate at sacrifice remained hyperglycaemic but also had the highest CSF lactate, the greatest cerebral sequestration and neurological depression, and biochemical and histological evidence of severe hepatic pathology. Serum cholesterol and corrected serum calcium fell consistently during infection; serum phosphate was also reduced in animals without renal impairment. These preliminary results indicate that lactic acidosis is a late complication of severe malaria and, by implication from this and other studies, hypoglycaemia occurs even later; other metabolic changes during P. coatneyi infection in rhesus monkeys also parallel those of severe falciparum malaria in humans. The model could be used in further studies of malaria-associated metabolic dysfunction and its management.

Title: Total parenteral nutrition without lipids in children during bone marrow transplantation
Abstract Note: Bone marrow transplantation (BMT) results in multiple toxicities and organ dysfunctions which significantly influence the nutritional status of patients. Conditioning regimen, which includes high-dose chemotherapy (with or without radiotherapy) may cause severe malnutrition due to stomatitis, nausea and vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, infections. Furthermore, graft versus host disease often contributes to malnutrition with gut lesions, atrophy and important diarrhea. Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is used as the most important nutritional support during the first month after transplantation. Twenty-five children undergoing BMT were studied to evaluate the efficacy of TPN without lipids in supporting nutritional status in the critical post BMT phase. Auxologic parameters, metabolic and biochemical and nutritional variables (albumin, prealbumin, transferrin) were determined in monitoring nutritional status and lipidemic parameters before and post NPT. We have observed a significant increase of triglycerides and apoprotein B and the decrease of cholesterol HDL and Apo Al. The efficacy of TPN, even without lipids, was documented by the good nutritional status (laboratory tests and weight) in all the patients. The infusion of TPN was not responsable for infection in any patient. The main complications of TPN were metabolic (hyperglycemia, hypopotassiemia, hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia) and were easily controlled.

Title: Vascular effects of diet-induced hypercalcemia after balloon artery injury in giant Flemish rabbits
Abstract Note: To determine whether metastatic calcification during neointima formation can result in neointimal calcification that simulates advanced human atherosclerosis, 32 giant Flemish rabbits (weight 5.5 ± 0.6 kg) underwent overstretch balloon injury of bilateral iliac arteries and received diet therapy for 8 weeks: high cholesterol (2%) and low calcium-vitamin D2 regimen (250 mg of calcium carbonate orally 5 times weekly and 50,000 U of calciferol intramuscularly 3 times weekly; group 1; n = 5); low cholesterol (0.5%) and high calcium-vitamin D2 regimen (500 mg of calcium carbonate orally 5 times weekly and 100,000 U of calciferol intramuscularly three times weekly; group 2; n = 19); or 0% cholesterol and high calcium-vitamin D2 regimen (group 3; n = 8). The incidence of vascular calcification was highest (71.4%) in group 2. Eighty-one percent of calcification was medial. Residual strain measurements of 7 thoracic aortas from group 2 compared to normal thoracic aortas from 8 control rabbits showed that residual strain was significantly increased in the calcified atherosclerotic aortas (12.3% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). We conclude that diet-induced hypercalcemia predominantly affects the media despite the presence of concomitant neointima formation from balloon artery injury with or without hypercholesterolemia and increases the residual strain more than twofold compared to normal thoracic aortas.

Title: Bone mineral density in patients with endogenous subclinical hyperthyroidism
Abstract Note: The aim of our study was to elucidate whether endogenous subclinical hyperthyroidism due to an autonomously functioning thyroid nodule affects bone metabolism and is a risk factor for osteoporosis and if so, whether it differs according to sex and menopausal status. In this cross-sectional study measurements of bone mineral density (BMD) were performed in 9 premenopausal, 12 post-menopausal women and it 7 men who had all endogenous subclinical hyperthyroidism due to an autonomously functioning thyroid nodule. Neither of them had a past history of hyperthyroidism not had been treated for any thyroid disorder. All of them were euthryroid by clinical and laboratory evaluation. They had single or multiple solid nodules or ultrasound and single or multiple autonomous (suppressing the surrounding tissue) nodules or scintigraphy. Lumbar spine BMD was measured by quantitative computerized tomography. The levels of triiodothyronine (T3), tetraiodothyronine (T4), free T3 (fT3), free T4 (fT4), thyrotropin (TSH), parathyroid hormone (PTH), serum calcium (Ca), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), cholesterol, ferritin, osteocalcin (OC) and urine calcium-creatinine ratios were determined. The results were compared with the age and sex matched controls in each subgroup (premenopausal, post-menopausal females and males). Bone mineral density of premenopausal females did not show any difference in comparison with age and sex matched controls. It was found to be significantly (p < 0.05) lower in post-menopausal females and insignificantly low in males when compared with age and sex matched controls. A statistically significant increase was found in OC levels in each of the three subgroup when compared with controls (p < 0.05). In conclusion, the results of our study revealed that endogenous subclinical hyperthyroidism due to an autonomously functioning thyroid nodule may affect bone metabolism and may be an additional risk factor for osteoporosis especially in post-menopausal females.

Title: Hormonal profile in abetalipoproteinemia
Abstract Note: In this study the pituitary, genitalia, adrenal, thyroid and parathyroid hormonal profile of a patient with abetalipoproteinemia (a woman aged 32), was investigated in two time periods (at the time of diagnosis of the disease and five years later), in order to see whether an almost complete absence of plasma LDL affects serum concentrations of various hormones. In our patient the concentrations of serum cortisol, Δ4, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S), 24 hour urine cortisol, progesterone, 17-OH progesterone, SHBG, estradiol, luteinizing hormone, follicle stimulating hormone, ACTH, T3, T4, TSH, FT3, FT4, parathormone, vitamin D3, testosterone, osteocalcine and prolactin were measured by radioimmunoassay. Ionized part of serum calcium was measured by the use of a special machine (CORNING), while bone alkaline phosphatase was measured by radioimmunoassay. The results revealed normal serum thyroid hormone levels as well as normal serum parathormone, FSH, LH, ACTH, testosterone, estradiol and SHBG levels. However, serum levels of prolactin were increased both in rest and during movement, while the levels of serum progesterone and 17-OH-progesterone were reduced. Estimation of serum progesterone was repeated on the 21st day of the menstrual cycle and was also found to be below the lowest normal limits. Despite the normal serum parathormone levels, serum ionizing calcium and 25-OH vitamin D were low, while the levels of serum bone alkaline phosphatase were increased. The results suggest that in patients with abetalipoproteinemia an impairement in the production of progesterone by the corpus luteum exists, probably due to the low levels of serum LDL and cholesterol, as well as an abnormal bone metabolism. The application of a modified diet does not influence the levels of serum progesterone and plasma ionized calcium. The function of the other endocrine glands is completely normal. We suggest the exogenous administration of progesterone in a case of gestation in a woman with abetalipoproteinemia independently of the nutrition status.

Title: Mechanisms of action of bisphosphonates
Abstract Note: Bisphosphonates (BPs) are pyrophosphate analogs in which the oxygen bridge has been replaced by carbon and diverse carbon side chains have generated a large family of compounds. Several are potent inhibitors of bone destruction (resorption) and are in clinical use for the treatment and prevention of osteoporosis, Paget's disease, hypercalcemia caused by malignancy, tumor metastases in bone, and other bone ailments. Selective action on bone is based on the binding of the BP moiety to the bone mineral. The molecular mode of action of BPs, which may differ from compound to compound, is unknown. However, at the tissue level, all BPs inhibit bone destruction and lead to an increase in bone mineral density by decreasing bone resorption and bone turnover. At the cellular level, the ultimate target of BP action is the osteoclast, the bone resorbing cell. In vitro evidence shows BP inhibition of osteoclast formation, via action on osteoblasts and there is in vitro and in vivo evidence for BP inhibition of osteoclast activity. There is in vivo and in vitro evidence for increased apoptosis. The relative contribution of these various effects on the therapeutic action of BPs remains to be established. At the molecular level, it is not known if BPs act on a single or multiple targets. Enzymes in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway and protein tyrosine phosphatases were shown to be inhibited by BPs.

Title: Analysis of blood biochemistry in normal Chinese full-term neonates
Abstract Note: In order to provide reference data of blood biochemical values in neonates, a prospective study on the blood biochemistry in Chinese neonates was performed. Forty-five healthy Chinese full-term neonates in the first three days of life were studied. The biochemistry included serum calcium, inorganic phosphate, glucose, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, cholesterol, total protein, albumin, total bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). The mean values of the blood biochemistry on three consecutive days were as follows; calcium: 8.94 ± 0.73, 8.44 ± 0.54 and 7.95 ± 0.66 mg/dl; inorganic phosphate: 5.39 ± O.41, 6.09 ± 0.81 and 6.45 ± 0.73 mg/dl; glucose: 64 ± 19, 75 ± 18 and 79 ± 12 mg/dl; BUN: 14.02 ± 3.19, 11.78 ± 3.47 and 9.24 ± 3.71 mg/dl; creatinine: 1.05 ± 0.31, 0.92 ± 0.23 and 0.75 ± 0.12 mg/dl, Uric acid: 7.08 ± 1.09, 5.10 ± 1.02 and 3.57 ± 0.88 mg/dl, cholesterol: 122 ± 22, 137 ± 21 and 152 ± 23 mg/dl; total protein: 5.54 ± 0.42, 5.71 ± 0.42 and 5.44 ± 0.41 g/dl; albumin: 3.48 ± 0.22, 3.14 ± 0.24 and 3.38 ± 0.21 g/dl; total bilirubin: 4.03 ± 0.41, 6.87 ± 1.68 and 7.89 ± 1.45 mg/dl; alkaline phosphatase: 120 ± 27, 129 ± 38 and 111 ± 32 U/L, LDH: 524 ± 91, 481 ± 73 and 426 ± 71 U/L; AST: 139 ± 82, 71 ± 28 and 49 ± 13 U/L; and ALT: 19.21 ± 7.19, 24.21 ± 15.77 and 18.94 ± 6.75 U/L. In conclusion, most of the biochemical parameters decreased as the infant got older, but inorganic phosphate, glucose, cholesterol and total bilirubin increased.

Title: Oral and intradialytic parenteral essenial amino acid therapy in hemodialysis patients with malnutrition
Abstract Note: After malnutrition has been seen to be an important factor of morbidity and mortality on hemodialysis patients, various oral and parenteral nutritional therapies have been developed to administrate to these patients. In this study, in order to investigate the effects of the oral and parenteral essential amino acid (EAA) therapy on the treatment of malnutrition in hemodialysis patients the half of 20 hemodialysis patients with malnutrition were treated with 0.9 gr/kg/week oral EAA (oral group) and the other half were treated with same dose parenteral EAA (parenteral group). Pretreatment and posttreatment values were compared by Wilcoxon T test in oral and parenteral groups. After these therapies, in both of the groups, there were no significant statistical increases in anthropometric parameters. While there were statistically significant increases in only serum calcium (p = 0.028) and lymphocyte counts (p = 0.028) in oral group, there were statistical significant increases in more parameters in parenteral group such as in serum albumin (p = 0.048), creatinine (p = 0.006), cholesterol (p = 0.006) levels and lymphocyte count (p = 0.006). These results suggest that parenteral EAA therapy is more comfortable and effective than oral EAA therapy in the treatment of hemodialysis patients with malnutrition.

Title: Smoking, arterial pressure and serum albumin are independent predictive factors of atherosclerosis in hemodialysis patients
Abstract Note: Objective: To investigate the relationship between atherosclerosis, arterial hypertension and other risk factors in uremic patients. Study design: A cross-sectional study in 119 dialysis patients (89 on hemodialysis and 30 on CAPD). Methods: Fasting blood sampling for serum lipids, albumin, hemoglobin, as well as echo-color-Doppler evaluation of common carotid arteries were performed in all patients (during the non-dialysis day in hemodialysis patients). Results: Ninety-five patients had at least one plaque and 57 had at least four plaques. Thirty-eight patients had mild and eleven subjects had severe carotid stenosis. In multiple regression models, the mean internal diameter of carotid arteries correlated to systolic pressure (β=0.36), serum cholesterol (β=-0.25), age (β=0.24) and smoking (β=0.17) (R=0.52, P=0.0001) while the degree of carotid stenosis was predicted by age (β=0.27) and smoking (β=0.23) (R=0.39, P=0.0001). Furthermore, the number of atherosclerotic plaques correlated by age (β=0.35), smoking (β=0.22) and pulse pressure (β=0.18) (R=0.51, P=0.0001) while serum albumin just failed to reach statistical significance (β=-0.16, P=0.06). However, in hemodialysis patients (n=89) serum albumin was a significant and independent predictor of the number of atherosclerotic plaques (β=-0.22). The Kt/Value, duration of dialysis treatment, hemoglobin, serum calcium and phosphate did not add any predictive power to the models. Conclusions: In dialysis patients arterial pressure and smoking are indipendent risk factors of atherosclerosis. Furthermore in hemodialysis patients, serum albumin is an independent predictor of atherosclerosis.

Title: Changes in bone and lipid metabolism in women with surgical menopause users and nonusers of estrogen replacement therapy
Abstract Note: We examined 60 women with surgical menopause, divided in two groups: group A (n=30), which started within a period of 1 to 6 months after the operation with sequential estrogen hormone replacement therapy (S E HRT): 3 weeks estradiol valerate 2 mg/day orally and after that 1 week pause without therapy, and group B (n=30), which was untreated after the operation with HRT (n=30). We estimated the following parameters: serum alkaline phosphatase (sAP), serum acid phosphatase (sAcP), serum calcium (sCa), serum phosphorus (sP), urinary calcium (uCa), urinary phosphorus (uP), urinary hydroxiproline (uHyPr), serum osteocalcin (sOc), ratio: urinary calcium/urinary creatinine (uCa/uCre), urinary phosphorus/urinary creatinine (uP/uCre) and urinary hydroxiproline/urinary creatinine (uHyPr/uCre), phosphorus index (PI), total lipids (TL), triglycerides (TG), beta lipoprotein units (BLU), degree of lipidemia (DL), total cholesterol (TC), cholesterol esters (CE), high density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-CH) and low density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-CH), before the therapy and after the first and sixth cycle (group A), and before and after one and six months of the operation (group B). In group A, we found that TL showed a very significant positive correlation with sAP, uP and uCa/uCre; TG with sAP and uCa/uCre; BLU with sAP and uCa/uCre; DL with uP/uCre; TC with uP; CE also with uP; LDL-CH with uP. On the other hand, HDL-CH showed a very significant negative correlation with sAcP and uP. We have to note that sCa showed a negative correlation with most of the parameters of lipid metabolism in this group. In group B we found that TL showed a very significant positive correlation with uHyPr; TG with sAP, sAcP, uP, sOC and PI; BLU with sAP, sAcP, uP, uCa/uCre, uHyP and sOC; DL with uCa and uHyP/uCre; TC with sAP, uCa, uP/uCre and PI; CE with sAP, sAcP, uP, uP/uCre and PI; LDL-CH with uCa, uP/uCre and PI. On the other hand, HDL-CH showed a very significant negative correlation with uCa and uP/uCre. We have to note that sCa showed a negative correlation with most of the parameters of lipid metabolism in this group. There is certain relationship between lipid and bone metabolism. We think that the flux of fatty acid through the liver and IGF-I, as a product of the liver, are the leading products in this relationship.
